Definition: {flesh (from its freshness); by extension, body, person; also (by euphemistically) the pudenda of a man}
BiblicalUsage: beshar is the word for flesh, and it appears 3 times across the Bible. Daniel says no flesh can reveal the king's dream, and the great tree gave meat for all.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe flesh is weak and cannot save itself, and that only God can reveal what no flesh can know. That is why I keep coming back to it: beshar is not a word to rush past.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
